item: Row 457 (R847): the feed entry's own date is kept for an article whose page gave none, and shown as the feed's
key_paths: src/ingest/feed_entry_date.py; src/ingest/pipeline.py; src/ingest/batch.py; src/backup/merge.py; src/api/main.py; src/static/app-core.js; migrations/versions/c2f6a8e4d1b7_article_feed_entry_date.py; tests/test_feed_entry_date_row457.py
summary: published_at came only from page metadata and the feed item's date was dropped (field analysis PR #2418: 6.6-9.0% of sampled sources have an undated article). The feed walk now reads each entry's published, then updated, date (UTC; refused when more than a day past the read) and keeps it in a new nullable column articles.feed_entry_published_at, only for a new article whose page gave no date of its own. It is never written into published_at, so no surface shows or charts it unless it reads it and flags it: the reader shows it as the feed's date with why on hover, and the article API rows, Home feed cards, both exports, the Latest panel and the evidence audit carry feed_entry_published_at and date_origin; the SPA draws every article date through one helper, ooArticleDateHtml. Time series keep using the article's own date only. Backups carry it: merge inserts it, adopts it onto a duplicate only when neither side has a date of its own and never replaces one; a backup from before the column restores with NULL through the migration chain. Migration and boot self-heal are one nullable ADD COLUMN, no backfill, no stored row rewritten. Strings x12.
